$meta.title: Church Organizational & Calling Hierarchy
$meta.source: General Handbook: Serving in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (December 2025 edition)
$meta.note: Section numbers below (e.g. '10.3') refer to General Handbook sections. Each 'nuances' entry is something that is NOT obvious from the calling title alone.

children.name: Presiding Bishopric
nuances: Each member holds the actual office of 'bishop' and is a General Authority — this is a completely different calling from a ward bishop, despite the shared title.
They administer temporal matters (welfare, finances, physical facilities, humanitarian efforts) for the ENTIRE Church, not a congregation.
Called by the First Presidency, not sustained locally like a ward bishop.

children.name: General Officers (Presidencies of Relief Society, Young Men, Young Women, Primary, Sunday School)
children.reports_to: First Presidency / Quorum of the Twelve / assigned General Authority Seventies
nuances: These are the only auxiliary organizations with a 'general' presidency layer above the stake — note 'Young Men' exists as a general organization name, but at the ward level there is no separate 'Young Men presidency' (see ward nuance below).
General Officers typically serve about five years, unlike most local callings which have no fixed term.

children.name: Area Presidency
members: Two Counselors (General Authority or Area Seventies)
nuances: Presides over stake AND mission presidents in the area — not just stakes.

children.name: Stake Presidency
nuances: The stake president is also, ex officio, the president of the stake high priests quorum (see nuance under High Council).

children.name: High Council
children.composition: 12 high priests called by the stake presidency
nuances: The high council does not meet as a body unless a member of the stake presidency is present to preside.
Individual high councilors are each assigned to a specific ward and to a specific elders quorum as the stake presidency's representative — this is a standing 1:1 assignment, not just committee work.

A high councilor can be authorized by the stake president to extend some callings, present members for sustaining, and set some members apart — i.e., high councilors can act with some of the stake presidency's calling authority.

children.name: Stake High Priests Quorum
nuances: This quorum is DIFFERENT from the ward-level elders quorum. Most ward high priests are NOT in this quorum — they're folded into their ward's elders quorum (see below). Only high priests currently serving in a stake presidency, bishopric, high council, or as patriarch belong to the stake high priests quorum.

children.name: Stake Patriarch
nuances: A patriarch cannot be called to a bishopric, high council, stake/mission/temple presidency without advance approval from the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. If approved, he's given 'not actively serving' patriarch status while he serves in the other calling.

children.name: Stake Executive Secretary
nuances: Works closely with the stake presidency but is NOT a member of it.

children.name: Stake Organizations (Relief Society, Young Women, Primary, Sunday School, Young Men)
nuances: The stake Sunday School president must be a sitting high councilor — unlike the other stake organization presidents.

The stake Young Men presidency is the ONLY stake organization presidency that does not hold its own annual stake leadership meeting; its instruction happens instead inside the stake priesthood leadership meeting alongside bishoprics and elders quorum presidencies.

These stake presidents/organizations exist ABOVE the ward organizations of the same name — do not confuse a 'stake Young Women president' with a ward's Young Women presidency; they're different callings at different levels.

children.name: Bishopric
children.called_by: Bishop by stake president (after First Presidency approval); counselors by stake president or assigned counselor
children.core_nuance: THE BISHOPRIC IS THE PRESIDENCY OF THE AARONIC PRIESTHOOD IN THE WARD — this is the specific nuance you flagged. There is no separate 'ward Young Men president' calling; the bishopric fills that functional role.
nuances: The bishop himself is, specifically, the president of the PRIESTS quorum (D&C 107:87) — not just a general overseer.
The First Counselor in the bishopric has direct responsibility for the TEACHERS quorum.
The Second Counselor in the bishopric has direct responsibility for the DEACONS quorum.
Whichever bishopric member attends a given Aaronic Priesthood quorum meeting presides in that meeting, regardless of which counselor 'owns' that quorum.
The bishopric also has foremost responsibility for young women (not just young men) as part of its 'rising generation' mandate, even though Young Women has its own ward presidency.
Only the bishop (not counselors, not the elders quorum president) counsels members on worthiness, abuse, and approval of fast-offering funds.

children.name: Ward Clerk / Assistant Ward Clerks
children.recommended_by: Bishop, approved by stake presidency and high council
nuances: Works closely with the bishopric but is explicitly NOT a member of the bishopric.
Is a member of ward council in his own right.
An assistant clerk assigned to finances must hold the Melchizedek Priesthood.

children.name: Ward Executive Secretary / Assistant Executive Secretaries
nuances: Also explicitly NOT a member of the bishopric, despite preparing agendas and scheduling for it.
Is a member of ward council.

children.name: Elders Quorum
children.president_called_by: Stake president (in consultation with the bishop) — NOT called by the bishop
children.core_nuance: The elders quorum is not just 'elders' — it absorbs nearly all ward high priests too.
nuances: Membership = all elders + all prospective elders + ALL high priests in the ward, EXCEPT those currently serving in a stake presidency, bishopric, high council, or as patriarch (those go to the stake high priests quorum instead).
The elders quorum president reports directly to the stake presidency (regular one-on-one meetings), while also receiving guidance from the bishop — he effectively has two lines of accountability.

A member of the elders quorum presidency may simply fill the role of 'ward mission leader' and/or 'ward temple and family history leader' — if so, he does NOT need to be separately called, sustained, or set apart for that role.
The elders quorum presidency partners directly with the Relief Society presidency (not the bishopric) to coordinate ministering assignments, missionary work, and temple/family history work.

children.name: Relief Society, Young Women, Primary, Sunday School Presidencies
children.president_recommended_and_called_by: Bishopric only (no stake presidency/high council approval step required)
nuances: Unlike the bishopric counselors, ward clerk, executive secretary, or elders quorum presidency — these four organization presidents and their counselors are entirely a ward-bishopric-level calling: recommended by the bishopric, approved by the bishopric, called by the bishop. The stake presidency isn't in this chain at all.

children.name: Aaronic Priesthood Quorums (Priests, Teachers, Deacons)

presidents.Priests Quorum: The bishop (he IS the president; he calls 1-2 priests as his 'assistants' rather than a separate quorum president)
presidents.Teachers Quorum: A teacher, called by a bishopric member (typically the First Counselor's area)
presidents.Deacons Quorum: A deacon, called by a bishopric member (typically the Second Counselor's area)

nuances: The priests quorum has no 'president' distinct from the bishop — his assistants are literally titled 'assistants,' not 'president/counselors.'
Youth quorum callings (deacons/teachers presidencies, priest assistants) are ANNOUNCED in sacrament meeting, not sustained by vote like adult callings.
Before extending any of these youth callings, the bishopric member must get the young man's parents' permission first.

children.name: Young Women (ward)
nuances: Young Women class presidents (or the whole presidency, if only one YW class exists) sit on the Ward Youth Council alongside the bishopric, a priests-quorum assistant, and the deacons/teachers quorum presidents.

children.name: Ward Council
nuances: The ward clerk and executive secretary are full standing members of ward council even though neither is a bishopric member.
Ward council members wear two hats simultaneously: (1) advisor for the whole ward, and (2) representative of their own organization — the handbook explicitly distinguishes these.

Distinct from 'Bishopric Meeting' (bishopric + clerk + executive secretary only, usually weekly) and 'Ward Youth Council' (a different, youth-focused meeting) — three separate standing meetings, easy to conflate.

children.name: Ward Mission Leader
nuances: Can be, and often is, the same person as a member of the elders quorum presidency — in which case no separate call/sustain/set-apart happens.

children.name: Ward Temple and Family History Leader
nuances: Same dual-role pattern as ward mission leader: may simply be a member of the elders quorum presidency, with no separate calling.

cross_cutting_nuances.detail: Who recommends → approves → sustains → sets apart varies by calling. Bishopric counselors, ward clerk, executive secretary, and elders quorum presidency all require stake presidency + high council approval. Relief Society/Young Women/Primary/Sunday School presidencies require ONLY bishopric approval — no stake involvement. This is the single biggest 'looks similar but isn't' trap when modeling calling workflows.

cross_cutting_nuances.topic: 'Not a member of the bishopric' callings
cross_cutting_nuances.detail: Ward clerk and executive secretary both work in lockstep with the bishopric, attend its meetings, and are sometimes assumed to be bishopric members by members — but the handbook is explicit that they are not.

'Young Men,' 'Young Women,' 'Relief Society,' 'Primary,' and 'Sunday School' presidencies all exist at BOTH the stake and ward level as distinct callings. A hierarchy model should namespace these by level (e.g., stake_relief_society_president vs ward_relief_society_president) to avoid collisions.
